study.kicker: Bachelor thesis · Virtual Design · Hochschule Kaiserslautern · 2026
study.subtitle: A digital pipeline for custom dental grillz
study.heroAlt: A render of the open gold grill on the teeth

grillz.heading: What are grillz, anyway?
body: Jewellery for the teeth: an accessory, a fashion piece, a statement, a status symbol, an investment, and one you put in and take out again.

Teeth differ from one person to the next. A ring can be passed on, and the next person wears it just as you did, if perhaps not on the same finger. A grill fits one set of teeth only. It is a one-off: individual and unique self-expression.

idee.heading: Where did the idea come from?
body: The cast of my teeth has stood on my desk for years. The orthodontist gave it to me when my treatment was over; otherwise it would have been thrown away.
And my favourite series is Breaking Bad, where one of the characters keeps a grill in a block of epoxy resin.

scan.heading: Where do I start?
body: With a scan of my teeth, of course. The orthodontist's cast is some years old, and I didn't want to rely on it alone.
Through my mother I knew that my dentist in Dansenberg has an intraoral scanner. A few emails later, there was an appointment to scan. The scans came back as STL files.
scan.credit: Scanned at Go-Dent Zahnärzte Kaiserslautern, Dr. Gehardt and Dr. Otter-Lorenz.

wissen.heading: What do I need to know?
body: I also talked to my dentist: what she thinks of it, what to look out for, how to go on from there.
Photogrammetry was out of the question.
wissen.learning: You have to work cleanly, because teeth are precious.

modell.heading: What comes next?
body: First the data. In Blender, the length unit is set to millimetres and the STL is imported at a scale of 0.001. Then the scan is cleaned up: floating vertices removed, broken teeth repaired.
Then the grill itself, in three steps: mask, extract, sculpt.
modell.cleanup: The scan before and after its clean-up.
modell.boolean: In Blender, with a Boolean against the jaw.

prototyp.heading: A first print
body: Before any metal, an FDM print: 3 g of filament and 30 minutes of printing. In the slicer the model is scaled to 101%, to make up for the shrinkage of PLA.
prototyp.slicer: Scaling in the slicer: 101% for PLA shrinkage.
prototyp.print: The print, under the printer's camera.

rendering.heading: Rendering
body: The renders come from Unreal Engine: a light setup, a grillz viewer built as a Blueprint, a material node tree, and three metals, silver, rose gold and gold, with flakes in the surface.
rendering.setup: The light setup, and the grillz viewer.

material.heading: Real-world materials
metals: Rose gold: a gold-copper alloy (Au & Cu)
material.lead: Not only a matter of looks, but medically justifiable and up to standard:
properties: Already established and tested in medicine
